output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates are not an operator problem. Printer records show every Veltranol job from 2 Jun to 3 Oct had a 24-month shelf life and a correct expiry. Every job from 4 Oct onward had a 36-month shelf life and a date 12 months too late. No operator overrides were made. The 4 jobs after the firmware change were correct, and so were the 3 run by agency operators. Two bad jobs ran on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a shelf life of 36 months for Veltranol, valid only from March 2027. The system should have ignored it until then, but the line data carried it from the next day. The vendor's claim that it cannot send future values is therefore contradicted by the records. Don't warn or remove the agency staff, and don't switch off the camera checks. Instead:
- Fix the ERP record.
- Extend the hold to all Veltranol lots since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
- Add a second-person check at setup.
- Check the other future-dated edits (HX-15-30 and MR-05-14).
- Ask the vendor why the future value was used.
Whether other products are affected is still unknown. A year-long reconciliation and over-labelling are premature until that is checked.
